This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of the Cr.P.C. seeking anticipatory bail in connection with FIR/Crime No.428/2024 dated 08.04.2024 registered at Police Anil Kumar Choubey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43378280/

sentences.text: It is contended by the counsel that in the present case the applicants are being subjected to double jeopardy inasmuch as, the complainant while alleging that there was demand of dowry at the behest of the applicants, lodged the report on 18/02/2024 i.e after one day of the scheduled date of marriage which has been brought on record as Annexure A/2 and a perusal of the same reflects that there are no allegation of taking of any cash or purchase of any household items towards dowry.

The entire FIR conspicuously silent as regards handing over the cheque and household items by the complainant side to the present applicants and the same did not suggest that there was any demand of dowry.
The present applicants after registration of the said case, moved an application for grant of bail.

The said application was also allowed vide order dated 04/04/2024 and after grant of bail to the present applicants, subsequently the FIR in question has been lodged against the present applicants on 08/04/2024.

If both the FIRs have been perused together, the same would reveal that handing over the alleged cash amount and household items are not mentioned in the previous FIR,
therefore, lodging of subsequent FIR is merely an afterthought as none of the events which are mentioned in the subsequent FIR has been mentioned in the previous FIR, thus, the present applicants deserves to be enlarged on anticipatory bail.
3 . The counsel for the State as well as objector has opposed the application submit that taking into consideration the serious allegations no case for grant of bail is made out.

The present applicants were paid cash of approximately Rs.7,22,000/- and also purchased other household items to satisfy the demand of dowry, therefore, the case has been rightly registered against the applicants.

Learned counsel for the objector submits that in terms of the decision of the Apex Court in the case of Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar and Ors. in Cr.A No.1277/2014 , it is for the applicants to cooperate with the investigation as in terms of Section 41 of Cr.P.C. they can very well enter their appearance as the punishment provided is less than seven years.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. Having considered the submissions advanced on behalf of the parties, a perusal of the FIR dated 18/02/2024 reflects that in the said FIR there are no allegations of taking cash of Rs.7,22,000/- and purchase of household items as dowry.

The previous FIR was lodged on 18/02/2024 and the subsequent FIR has been lodged on 08/04/2024 and the events in the subsequent FIR pertains to the period prior to 18/02/2024, therefore, prima facie as in the previous FIR the allegations which are mentioned in subsequent FIR are missing, this Court deems it appropriate to enlarge the applicants on anticipatory bail, therefore, without commenting on the merit of the case, the application is allowed.

6. It is directed that in the event of arrest, applicants shall be enlarged on bail on furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) each with one surety each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer for his appearance before him during the course of investigation or before the trial Court concerned during trial, as the case may be.
7.

It is further directed that the applicant shall abide by all the conditions as enumerated under Section 438(2) of the Cr.P.C.
